verses.verse:
जिह्वावतींम् सुजिह्वां तु मुखाग्रेण निनादयेत्।
मध्यतार परीक्षाया मुत्तीर्णाम् सरस, स्वराम्।७३।
verses.text: The Jihvāvatī (duct bānsurī) with a good jihvā (fipple) should be sounded with the front of the mouth; [it should be one] that has passed the test of the middle and high [registers] and has sweet notes.

commentary.text: In the āḍī (transverse) bānsurī or the Tripurā bānsurī the sweetness of the breath depends on the practitioner, but in the Jihvāvatī (duct bānsurī) the sweetness of the breath depends mostly on the maker, and making it is somewhat difficult. So it will be best, for the most part, to buy a bānsurī with a jībh (fipple) from the market, because that maker's hand is practised in making it. Even so, the faults that are possible should be tested for at the time of buying. If there is no hissing in the breath and all seven notes come out properly in both octaves, it will be right to buy such a bānsurī from the market and play it. While playing, only the front part of the mouth should touch it; and, avoiding again and again faults of posture such as puffing the cheeks and shutting the eyes, one should practise on the notes of both octaves with the help of 'ṭa' or 'ka' on the tongue. Now some light is thrown on the rakhāva (placement) of the fingers.

subsection.title: Practice of the Tongue and of the Fingers
